newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes mixed amid optimism for Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes mixed amid optimism for Pakistan.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed, underpinned by optimism for a large sale of U.S. wheat this weekend to Pakistan and prospects for further sales of wheat to Asian customers, traders said.
But Canadian logistical problems rattled the market.
"The Pakistan tender is supporting it but the Canadian thing isn't helping," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Traders said Pakistan will likely buy 450,000 tonnes of wheat Sunday from the U.S. The Australian Wheat Board on Friday said Australia's brisk shipping program and ensuing logistics may keep it from offering wheat to Pakistan.
The wheat market was stirred early Friday by news Canada may seek to ship wheat through U.S. ports. Traders said that scenario, if accomplished, would be bearish for U.S. wheat.
But the market remained poised for a slight hike in U.S. wheat exports over the near term with Asia targeted.

"Logistics are particularly restrictive for Canada and Australia. If you need quick shipment wheat for export you buy it here, particularly if it's for Asian customers and for West Coast loading," a trader said.
Wheat closed 1/2 cent per bushel higher to 1/4 lower, with March up 1/2 at $3.59-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 12,000 contracts, below the 17,195 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc sold 100 July $3.80 calls at 6-1/4, Cargill Investor Services bought 100 March $3.90 calls and sold 100 March $3.40 puts, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,500 contracts, below the 3,804 traded Thursday.
